messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013524/pdf/nihms-2073793.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/acsnano.3c10070

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Automated Cartridge-Based Cancer Early Screening System (ACCESS) - Droplet Magnetofluidic, Methylation-on-Beads (MOB) Assay with Methylation-Specific qPCR (qMSP) for DNA Methylation Cancer Biomarker Detection

REAGENTS USED:
  - Sample (patient tissue lysate, extracted gDNA, or cultured cell pellet, loaded into the cartridge's sample port)
  - Magnetic Beads (silica superparamagnetic MagBinding beads that bind nucleic acids for magnetic transport between reagent droplets)
  - Conversion Reagent (Lightning Conversion Reagent, used with thermolabile proteinase K for tissue digestion, DNA denaturation, and bisulfite sulfonation/deamination of unmethylated cytosines)
  - Proteinase K (thermolabile proteinase K, digests sample and self-inactivates with heat, preventing qPCR inhibition from spillover)
  - Binding Buffer (M-Binding buffer, mediates DNA-silica bead conjugation)
  - Wash Buffer (200 mM NaCl, 10% w/v PEG 6000, 0.1% Tween 20, used across three wash droplets to remove unbound reagent from the beads while remaining anchored in the cartridge's wash wells)
  - Desulfonation Buffer (L-desulfonation buffer, completes bisulfite conversion by removing sulfonate groups from converted DNA)
  - qPCR Mix (200 nM methylation-specific forward/reverse primers, Platinum Taq polymerase, EvaGreen Plus dye, dNTPs, MgCl2, and custom qPCR buffer, contained in the final droplet where DNA is eluted off the beads and amplified)

STEPS:
1. Sample mixture preparation: The patient sample (lysed tissue, extracted DNA, or cell pellet) is mixed with silica magnetic beads, bisulfite conversion reagent, and thermolabile proteinase K, then loaded into the cartridge's sample port.
2. Sample digestion: The cartridge is inserted into the instrument, and the sample mixture is incubated at 30 C for 45 min in the first thermally isolated well to digest the sample and extract genomic DNA.
3. DNA denaturation: The extracted DNA is incubated at 98 C for 8 min to denature the DNA in preparation for bisulfite conversion.
4. Sulfonation and deamination: The denatured DNA is incubated at 58 C for 60 min, selectively converting unmethylated cytosines to uracils while methylcytosines remain unconverted (the core bisulfite conversion chemistry).
5. DNA-bead binding: M-Binding buffer is added and incubated at room temperature for 10 min, binding the DNA to the silica magnetic beads so it can be magnetically transferred between wells.
6. First wash: The motorized magnet array transfers the DNA-bound beads into a wash droplet to remove unbound sample components.
7. Desulfonation: The washed, DNA-bound beads are transferred into the desulfonation droplet, completing bisulfite conversion of the DNA.
8. Second and third washes: The DNA-bound beads are transferred through two more wash droplets to remove residual desulfonation reagent.
9. Elution into qPCR droplet: The washed beads are transferred into the final qPCR droplet, where the bisulfite-converted DNA is directly eluted off the beads by incubation at 70 C for 10 min; the (now DNA-free) beads are then magnetically transferred out of and upstream from the qPCR droplet to avoid interfering with fluorescence detection.
10. Methylation-specific qPCR: The eluted, bisulfite-converted DNA undergoes 45 cycles of methylation-specific qPCR thermocycling (103 C for 5 s denaturation, 63 C for 15 s annealing/extension), with only methylated-cytosine-derived sequences available for primer amplification.
11. Fluorescence detection and readout: Between each thermocycle, the optical module's motorized fiber sequentially scans each of the four cartridge channels to acquire the EvaGreen Plus fluorescence signal, and upon assay completion the instrument sends the resulting amplification curve data over USB to a laptop for Cq analysis and display.

INTERPRETATION: Successful methylation biomarker detection is confirmed by a qPCR amplification curve (fluorescence vs. cycle number) crossing a quantification threshold to yield a cycle of quantification (Cq) value; a positive (methylated) sample shows amplification (lower Cq) while a true-negative (unmethylated/normal) sample shows no amplification even after 55 cycles in later validation runs. Using this platform, the housekeeping gene ACTB was consistently detected on-cartridge (mean Cq 24.46 from spiked bisulfite-converted DNA; mean Cq 27.32 from raw gDNA), the esophageal cancer methylation biomarkers TAC1 and ZNF132 were detected down to 1% methylated DNA in a nonmethylated DNA background, and both markers were successfully detected in tumor tissue/DNA from ESCC patients while remaining negative in paired normal tissue, supporting ACCESS as a portable, automated diagnostic tool for early esophageal cancer detection in resource-constrained settings.

module fluorescence

manifest Sample
manifest MagneticBeads
manifest ConversionReagent
manifest ProteinaseK
manifest BindingBuffer
manifest WashBuffer
manifest DesulfonationBuffer
manifest qPCRMix

instructions:

sample = dispense 1 units of Sample
beads = dispense 1 units of MagneticBeads
conv = dispense 1 units of ConversionReagent
protk = dispense 1 units of ProteinaseK

a = mix sample with beads
b = mix a with conv
mixture = mix b with protk

heat mixture at 30c for 45m
heat mixture at 98c for 8m
heat mixture at 58c for 60m

binding = dispense 1 units of BindingBuffer
bound = mix mixture with binding for 10m

wash1 = dispense 1 units of WashBuffer
temp1 = mix bound with wash1 for 60s
dispose temp1

desulf = dispense 1 units of DesulfonationBuffer
desulfonated = mix bound with desulf for 60s

wash2 = dispense 1 units of WashBuffer
temp2 = mix desulfonated with wash2 for 60s
dispose temp2

wash3 = dispense 1 units of WashBuffer
temp3 = mix desulfonated with wash3 for 60s
dispose temp3

qpcrmix = dispense 1 units of qPCRMix
droplet = mix desulfonated with qpcrmix for 5s

heat droplet at 70c for 10m

repeat 45 times {
    heat droplet at 103c for 5s
    heat droplet at 63c for 15s
}

signal = detect fluorescence on droplet for 5s

if (signal >= 1) {
    dispose droplet
}

dispose droplet

identity.protocol_name: Cancer Methylation Biomarker Detection in an Automated, Portable, Multichannel Magnetofluidic Platform (Hasnain, Stark, Trick, Ma, Hsieh, Cheng, Meltzer & Wang, ACS Nano 2024)

source.title: Automated Cartridge-Based Cancer Early Screening System (ACCESS) - Droplet Magnetofluidic, Methylation-on-Beads (MOB) Assay with Methylation-Specific qPCR (qMSP) for DNA Methylation Cancer Biomarker Detection

ir.content:
main:
	sample1[0] = dispense(Sample)
	beads1[0] = dispense(MagneticBeads)
	conv1[0] = dispense(ConversionReagent)
	protk1[0] = dispense(ProteinaseK)
	a1[0] = mix(sample1[0], beads1[0])
	b1[0] = mix(a1[0], conv1[0])
	mixture1[0] = mix(b1[0], protk1[0])
	heat(mixture1[0]) @ 30.0CELSIUS @ 2700.0SECOND
	heat(mixture1[0]) @ 98.0CELSIUS @ 480.0SECOND
	heat(mixture1[0]) @ 58.0CELSIUS @ 3600.0SECOND
	binding1[0] = dispense(BindingBuffer)
	bound1[0] = mix(mixture1[0], binding1[0]) @ 600.0SECOND
	wash11[0] = dispense(WashBuffer)
	temp11[0] = mix(bound1[0], wash11[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	dispose(temp11[0])
	desulf1[0] = dispense(DesulfonationBuffer)
	desulfonated1[0] = mix(bound1[0], desulf1[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	wash21[0] = dispense(WashBuffer)
	temp21[0] = mix(desulfonated1[0], wash21[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	dispose(temp21[0])
	wash31[0] = dispense(WashBuffer)
	temp31[0] = mix(desulfonated1[0], wash31[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	dispose(temp31[0])
	qpcrmix1[0] = dispense(qPCRMix)
	droplet1[0] = mix(desulfonated1[0], qpcrmix1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	heat(droplet1[0]) @ 70.0CELSIUS @ 600.0SECOND
bsbbr_2_h:
	PHI REPEAT_451 = {REPEAT_450,REPEAT_452}
	PHI droplet2 = {droplet1,droplet2}
	if REPEAT_451[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_3_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_4_f
bsbbr_3_t:
	heat(droplet2[0]) @ 103.0CELSIUS @ 5.0SECOND
	heat(droplet2[0]) @ 63.0CELSIUS @ 15.0SECOND
	REPEAT_452[0] = REPEAT_451[0] - 1
bsbbr_4_f:
	signal1[0] = detect(fluorescence, droplet2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	if signal1[0] >= 1	|	true: jump bsbbif_5_t	|	false: jump bsbbif_6_f
bsbbif_5_t:
	dispose(droplet2[0])
bsbbif_6_f:
	PHI droplet3 = {droplet2,droplet}
	dispose(droplet3[0])
	NOP

numeric_mismatches.note: The Results and Discussion text and Materials and Methods each state 45 qPCR cycles for cartridge characterization runs, but the Materials and Methods 'ACCESS Testing' paragraph states 55 cycles for the full clinical ACCESS testing runs (consistent with the 'even after 55 qPCR cycles' language used for negative controls elsewhere in Results). 45 was used here as the value explicitly tied to the reported total qPCR duration ('45-cycle qPCR to be completed in 45 min'); 55 cycles would be the more literal match for the full clinical protocol described in Materials and Methods.

Materials and Methods: ACCESS Testing states 55 C for 60 min for sulfonation/deamination, while the Portable Instrumentation section states the sample incubator delivers 58 C for this step. 58C was used here as the value from the instrument-characterization section; 55C is the alternate value from the testing-protocol paragraph.

numeric_mismatches.field: wash steps modeled as mix(bead-complex, WashBuffer)/dispose rather than physical magnetic transfer between wells
numeric_mismatches.note: In the paper, DNA-bound beads are physically transported by a motorized magnet array between separate thermally and kinetically isolated wells of the cartridge, with each wash droplet a distinct stationary reservoir. BioScript has no magnetic-transport-between-wells primitive, so this is approximated as sequential mix/dispose operations on a single continuous bead-complex variable.

No literal numeric fluorescence threshold is stated in the paper; qPCR positivity is instead determined by a four-parameter logistic regression fit to derive a Cq (cycle of quantification) value after baseline correction (Figure S11). The 'signal >= 1' condition is a stand-in for a generic amplification/no-amplification classification, not a reported cutoff.

numeric_mismatches.field: magnet arm biaxial actuation (servo/stepper motors), Peltier thermal module PID control, motorized optical fiber scanning across 4 channels, Arduino microcontroller coordination, cartridge fabrication (PETG/PMMA/PTFE layers), 4-plex parallel channel operation
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are hardware-control, device-fabrication, or multichannel-parallelization details of the instrument itself, not part of the single-channel reagent-handling MOB assay sequence, and fall outside the scope of this translation.

The assay is performed on a qPCR Thermocycler platform. Key reagents used in the assay include Sample and Magnetic Beads.
